candidates.title: MetaStep.step, the step library's documented top-level transition verifier, is a second verifier path whose counter-to-form map differs from Dave's and the manual's (reset on the first uarch cycle instead of the last, no delivery form)
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, generated code regenerated from audit/prt2 (MetaStep.sol; byte-identical in released/, regenerated-patched/ and dave/released/machine/step/src/)
candidates.role: Referee verifier by the AUDIT.md component table (machine-solidity-step as a whole). By THREAT_MODEL section 3 it is arguably a support copy, because the pinned Dave CartesiStateTransition does not import MetaStep, so its acceptance settles nothing in the pinned deployment. Both readings are given below.
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/MetaStep.sol MetaStep.step(counter, accessLogs): runs UArchStep.step, then UArchReset.reset iff counter == (counter >> 20) << 20, i.e. counter % 2^20 == 0. No SendCmioResponse path. released/README.md 'Step function' describes MetaStep.step as 'the top-level state transition function, it is meant to take the machine from state s[i] to state[i + 1]' and says it resets 'every 1 << ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_UARCH_CYCLES_PER_MCYCLE cycles'. Compare dave/released/prt/contracts/src/state-transition/CartesiStateTransition.sol transitionState: step+reset iff (counter & UARCH_CYCLE_MASK) == UARCH_CYCLE_MASK, delivery+step iff (counter & INPUT_MASK) == 0, where counter is the index of the before-state. The manual's validate_state_transition_response (doc/README.md 'Settling a match', doc/recipes/prt.lua) does the same: reset iff uarch_cycle == UARCH_CYCLE_MAX, delivery iff state_transition_offset == 0 and input_period_offset == 0 and an input exists.
candidates.description: The regenerated step library ships two verifier entry points for the same transitions: the per-form libraries that Dave composes, and MetaStep.step, which the library documents as THE state transition function from s[i] to s[i+1]. MetaStep maps a position to a form differently. (a) With counter = i, the index of the before-state, which is the convention of the README sentence, of Dave's transitionState and of the manual, it applies the uarch reset after the FIRST uarch step of each mcycle (uarch_cycle 0) and never after the last one (uarch_cycle UARCH_CYCLE_MAX). (b) Under any counter convention it has no input-delivery form: at the opening of an input slot that holds an input it verifies only a uarch step. The threat model makes the map from position to transition form a referee parameter (section 2 'Transition form ... The position, the dispute constants, and the on-chain input record determine it') and R11 requires 'Every transition form has exactly one verifier path'. A referee built on the library's documented top-level function (rather than on hand composition as Dave does) accepts wrong after-hashes from reachable states and rejects honest proofs. The harness's own smoke test (bugs/harness/solidity-step/evm/smoke.lua) uses counter = i+1 for MetaStep, which is the only reading under which the reset placement is right, so the reset placement depends on an undocumented off-by-one convention that contradicts the README. The delivery form is missing under either reading.
candidates.trigger: Any party that submits a step proof to a referee that uses MetaStep.step: a dishonest claimant submits step+reset at uarch_cycle 0, or a step-only log at an input opening. The honest operator's proofs are rejected at uarch_cycle UARCH_CYCLE_MAX and at input openings.
candidates.reachability: Reachable before-states. Case (a) uses baremetal-minimal at an mcycle boundary with the uarch in its pristine reset state, which every run passes through at every mcycle. Case (b) uses baremetal-template, a valid template waiting at an rx-accepted manual yield. In the pinned Dave deployment MetaStep is not reached: CartesiStateTransition calls SendCmioResponse, UArchStep and UArchReset directly. So the defect is live only for a deployment or tool that uses MetaStep as its transition verifier, as the step library's README directs.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a crafted proof, which section 4 puts in scope ('Logs and proofs are adversarial'). It needs no excluded condition, unless the triager reads MetaStep as dead code of the referee component; then step 2 applies. 2. Role: AUDIT.md lists 'machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2' as 'Referee verifier'. Section 3 defines 'Referee verifier. A verifier whose acceptance settles disputes, such as the on-chain verifiers' and 'Support ... copies of the verifiers whose acceptance settles nothing'. MetaStep's acceptance settles nothing in pinned Dave, so the section-3 reading makes it support. 3. High/Medium cases: as support, section 3 says 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier'. In the referee-verifier role it would be Critical (step 4), so under the support reading it is Medium. 4. Critical under the component-table reading: it matches the listed Critical case 'A verifier defect that lets some log be accepted, for a reachable before-state, with an after-hash other than the canonical one' (counter=0 accepts step+reset with an after-hash other than the canonical one), and it violates R11 'Every transition form has exactly one verifier path', R3 'Every log that a verifier accepts must then yield ... the canonical hash' and R4 (honest step+reset and delivery proofs are rejected). 5. Not needed. Which reading applies depends on whether a deployment uses MetaStep. The pinned one does not, so the section-3 reading gives Medium.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support copy of the referee verifier). Critical if triage applies the AUDIT.md table role of machine-solidity-step to MetaStep.
candidates.threat_to_goal: A referee that uses the step library's documented top-level transition function settles wrong states. At uarch_cycle 0 a dishonest claim proves step+reset to a state that skips the rest of the instruction. At input openings it proves a step without the delivery, which drops the input. The honest claim cannot prove the true closing transition or the true delivery, so it is eliminated (soundness and completeness failures, section 1). In the pinned Dave deployment the goal holds only because Dave composes the forms by hand. The library still violates R11 by shipping a divergent second verifier path for the same forms.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R11/metastep.lua against the shared EVM harness (StepVerifier over the regenerated step, anvil at 127.0.0.1:8546, eth_call only). (1) baremetal-minimal at pristine uarch: metaStep(counter=0, honest step log) reverts 'Write region root doesn't match'. metaStep(counter=0, step log + reset log) is accepted with root 0x99d67139fb55aad4..., while the canonical after-hash of that transition (one uarch step) is 0x2754a339ac24db18... (2) After run_uarch(UARCH_CYCLE_MAX), the honest step+reset at counter = 2^20-1 (Dave's index of the closing transition) reverts 'buffer should be fully consumed'. (3) baremetal-template (valid template waiting for input): metaStep(counter=1, step-only log) is accepted with 0xa6f7bf8f8873acb4..., while the delivery+step after-hash for an input 'x' is 0x010ab25c7000c962... diff -rq confirms that MetaStep.sol in dave/released/machine/step/src, released/ and regenerated-patched/ is identical.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua using evm_step: on baremetal-minimal, assert that metaStep(root, 0, step_log ++ reset_log) is rejected, or equals the canonical after-hash, and that metaStep(root, 2^20-1, step_log ++ reset_log) is accepted and equals m:get_root_hash() after step+reset. On baremetal-template, assert that metaStep cannot accept a step-only log at an input-opening counter. Expected to exit 1 now and 0 once MetaStep follows Dave's counter-to-form map, including delivery, or is removed.

candidates.title: verify_step (C, Lua and JSON-RPC) takes the hash function from the step log header; the verifier API has no referee-supplied hash function
candidates.component: Off-chain verifier: machine::verify_step / cm_verify_step / Lua machine.verify_step / JSON-RPC machine.verify_step, with replay_step_state_access
candidates.role: Support (the off-chain verify functions, per the AUDIT.md table). The main-processor step log is the proof form used for ZK proving, which is out of scope ('Disputes settled by other proof forms, such as a step of the main processor verified inside a proof system, are outside its scope').
candidates.location: src/replay-step-state-access.hpp, replay_step_state_access constructor (about lines 156-200): reads a uint64 hash-function field from the log header and sets m_context.hash_function to keccak256 or sha256. compute_root_hash and every page and node hash then use it. src/machine.cpp machine::verify_step (about line 2313) and src/cm.cpp cm_verify_step take no hash-function argument, and neither do src/jsonrpc-remote-machine.cpp jsonrpc_machine_verify_step_handler and src/clua-i-machine.cpp machine_obj_index_verify_step.
candidates.description: R11 requires 'Each deployment fixes one hash function, which no proof can select'. verify_step lets the log (the proof) select keccak256 or sha256. The verifier compares the logged before-hash with the caller's before-hash, but which function computes the pages, the siblings and the after-hash comes from the log. The caller has no way to pin the deployment's function. The uarch verifiers (verify_step_uarch, verify_reset_uarch, verify_send_cmio_response) hard-code keccak256 and are not affected. In practice the selection gives no forgery without a cross-function preimage, because the top-level concat must still equal the referee's before-hash. That is why this rates low.
candidates.trigger: A party that supplies a step log to a caller of verify_step, choosing the header's hash-function field.
candidates.reachability: Any before-state. Both hash functions verify through the same API call (see evidence).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: probably, as ZK proving (AUDIT.md 'Not in scope: ZK proving'; THREAT_MODEL intro). The main-processor step log is the ZK proof form. 2. Role: off-chain verify functions are 'Support' in AUDIT.md. 3. High/Medium: a support defect is Medium only 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. Even as a referee verifier, selecting the function gives no acceptance of a wrong after-hash without breaking a hash primitive (THREAT_MODEL 7: 'The adversary is not assumed to break the hash functions'), so it would not rate High or Critical. 4. Not Critical: no reachable wrong acceptance. 5. Low: it violates R11's wording ('which no proof can select') with no demonstrated effect.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (or Out of scope as ZK proving)
candidates.threat_to_goal: No direct threat to the goal. It breaks R11's principle that the hash function is a referee parameter, so any future verifier built on this API, for example a ZK guest that takes the deployment's function from elsewhere, inherits a proof-selected parameter.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R11/vstep3.lua: on baremetal-minimal recreated with fresh hash trees under keccak256 and under sha256, m:log_step(1, f) followed by cartesi.machine:verify_step(before, f, 1) is accepted for both and returns the machine's root hash. The verify call is identical in both cases, so the log alone chose the function.
candidates.test_idea: Write a sha256 step log for a keccak deployment's verifier call and assert that verify_step refuses it once the API takes the hash function as a parameter. The current API cannot express the requirement, so the test asserts that a keccak-pinned verify entry exists and rejects a header that says sha256.

candidates.title: A machine can be re-instantiated under a different hash function while reusing hash-tree data computed under the original one (the hash function is not bound to the cached tree)
candidates.component: Machine creation from a configuration (machine API, hash tree)
candidates.role: Honest operator only if a production node plausibly does this. More likely a trusted-caller misuse off the honest operator's path.
candidates.location: Machine construction from a machine_config whose hash_tree.hash_function differs from the function that wrote hash_tree.sht/.phtc and the per-range .dht/.dpt files it references (get_initial_config() of a stored machine with hash_tree.hash_function changed). src/machine-config.hpp hash_tree.hash_function. The cached tree files carry no hash-function tag that creation checks.
candidates.description: Taking get_initial_config() of a stored keccak machine, setting hash_tree.hash_function='sha256' and creating a machine from it succeeds. The new machine reuses the keccak .sht/.dht data (mark_pages_dirty=false) under sha256. Its root hash is then neither the keccak nor the sha256 content hash: get_proof(0x80000000, 12).target_hash differs from the sha256 root of the page's contents. verify_hash_tree() returns true on a fresh instance and false after some queries ('page ... is not marked dirty but is dirty'). R11's clause 'Every machine it disputes uses that hash function for life' and R9 are only enforced by convention.
candidates.trigger: The trusted machine-API caller creating a machine from a config that changes the hash function but keeps the stored hash-tree files.
candidates.reachability: Requires a deliberate config edit by the trusted caller. Loading a directory with cartesi.machine(dir) keeps the stored function, so the plain load path is not affected.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: likely. THREAT_MODEL 8 excludes 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented', and defects that need cached hash-tree data to survive adoption without a rebuild (O1). Section 2: cached hash-tree data is 'outside the state hash, and loading does not check it'. 2. Role: machine API; the honest operator only if a node does this, which seems implausible. 3. Medium candidate: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree ... inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)', if the manual documents creating a machine from a stored machine's config with a changed hash function. I did not find such documentation. 4. Not Critical: not on the honest operator's path. 5. Otherwise Low ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller').
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if triage finds the operation documented)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly. A tool that switched a template's hash function this way would compute a root that no verifier reproduces. Creation could refuse cached tree data whose function differs from the config's.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R11/sha.lua and sha4.lua: with the reused files, verify_hash_tree() went true and then false, and the page-root mismatch was reported. With the files stripped (vstep3.lua, sha3.lua), the sha256 tree is consistent and log_step works.
candidates.test_idea: Create a machine from a stored keccak machine's initial config with hash_function=sha256 and assert that creation fails, or that get_root_hash() equals the sha256 root recomputed from contents (verify_hash_tree() true after get_proof queries).

UArchStep.sol and UArchReset.sol instruction semantics versus uarch-step.cpp: R2/R3, not R11. Only AccessLogs.sol, Buffer.sol, SendCmioResponse.sol and MetaStep.sol were read for parameter handling.
Whether ArbitrationConstants (levels 2, log2step [38,0], height [54,38]) satisfy A7 sizing: only checked that 54+38 = 24+48+20 and that the level-1 span equals one level-0 leaf.
prt-bridge.lua, prt-ethereum.lua, prt-epoch.lua, prt-deploy.lua (support): proof encoding to Dave was not audited for parameter selection beyond evm_step's matching encoder.

prtu.lua wire protocol and the decoding of hashes, integers and tables from player responses (type confusion such as float positions or non-string hashes) in the referee model: only spot-checked through keccak argument checks and verify_slice.
vg.lua/vgu.lua (verification-game referee): only confirmed that its validate_state_transition_response matches the manual. Its bisection validation was not checked.
Cartesi Rollups InputBox input-size limit and A3 (no input larger than the delivery proof allows) versus CanonicalMachine.INPUT_MAX_SIZE = 1<<16: noted, not verified.
JSON-RPC verify handlers: only checked that they take no proof-selected hash function or form. Their argument decoding was not fuzzed.
The ZK step path (zk_merkle_tree_hash hooks) beyond the hash-function header: out of scope.
machine-guest-tools: not relevant to R11, not examined.
